language_wrapper: A rectangular grid maze has {rows} rows and {cols} columns of unit squares. For each middle row (that is, rows 2 through {rows_minus_two_plus_one}), there is exactly one invisible teleportation gate hidden in that row, and no two gates lie in the same column. An explorer may start each attempt from any chosen square in the top row. In an attempt, the explorer may move one square at a time up, down, left, or right, revisiting squares if desired. If the explorer steps on a teleportation gate, the attempt immediately ends and the explorer is returned to the starting square of that attempt; the exact gate location just triggered is then recorded and remembered for future attempts. If the explorer reaches any square in the bottom row, they immediately succeed and the process stops. Give a general strategy that guarantees success in the worst case by the k-th attempt, no matter how the gates are placed subject to the rules, and find the minimum possible value of k in terms of {rows} and {cols}.
hardness_rationale: The family extends the seed from a single fixed size (3033 × 3032) to any tight rectangular maze with rows r and columns r−1, demanding a uniform proof valid for all sizes. Proving optimality (both upper and lower bounds) for arbitrary r in this extremal constraint regime requires a more general and delicate adversarial argument and a size-independent construction of the 3-attempt strategy. This abstraction enforces reasoning about arbitrary injective row-to-column placements and path reconfiguration across attempts, which is more involved than solving a single numeric instance.
notes: This parametric version preserves the key extremal difficulty cols = rows − 1 that makes the 3-attempt bound both tight and nontrivial. The verifier enforces this tight regime to avoid degenerate cases that might allow fewer attempts via column slack.
source_question: An explorer is challenging to pass through a maze composed of 3033 rows and 3032 columns of squares. The rules of the maze are as follows: In all the middle rows (that is, from the 2nd row to the 3032nd row), there is one invisible teleportation gate hidden in each row, and there are no multiple invisible teleportation gates in the same column. The explorer starts from any position in the 1st row. Each time, he can move one square up, down, left or right, and it is allowed to pass through the explored areas repeatedly. If the explorer touches a teleportation gate, he will immediately return to the starting point and start the next attempt. However, the explorer will mark the position of that teleportation gate. If the explorer reaches any position in the 3033rd row, he will directly pass the maze. It is known that the explorer can remember the positions of all the discovered teleportation gates. Please construct a general strategy so that no matter how the teleportation gates are distributed, the explorer will definitely pass the maze in the \(k\)th attempt in the worst-case scenario. Find the minimum possible value of \(k\).
